title.narrative: Water Services and Institutional Support Project II

description.narrative: The objectives of the Project are to: (i) Increase water service coverage in key cities of Mozambique's territory; (ii) Strengthen the institutional and regulatory capacity for water supply services in the northern, central and southern regions of Mozambique's territory; and (iii) Support Mozambique to respond promptly and effectively to an Eligible Crisis or Emergency.

The objectives of the Second Water Services and Institutional Support Project are to: (a) increase water service coverage in key cities in Mozambique's territory; (b) strengthen the institutional and regulatory capacity for water supply services in the Northern, Central and Southern regions of Mozambique; and (c) support Mozambique to respond promptly and effectively to an Eligible Crisis or Emergency. There are five components to the project, the first component being rehabilitation and expansion of water supply production and distribution. The second component is the Institutional Support. This component will also support project management, supervision for contracts under component one, audits, training, and various technical studies as needed, as well as technical assistance to FIPAG for the implementation of environmental and social safeguards. The third component is the output-based payments for low-income-household connections. The objective of the component is to increase access to piped-water connections for low-income households in the cities of the central and northern regions of the recipient and in the Maputo region by providing output-based payments to the regional utilities to support the provision of water services to the poor by facilitating the uptake of connections for low-income households through grant payments to reimburse the costs of eligible connections. Finally, the fourth component is the contingent emergency response (zero-budget).

title.narrative: New piped household water connections that are resulting from the project intervention

comment.narrative: Target achieved (133%). This indicator measured the number of new connections installed, including poor household connections and new connections under the CERC. The target was increased with the AF to reflect connections in Nacala. The result reflects: 30,789 new water connections in the Beira-Dondo system, 18,070 new water connections in the Tete-Moatize system, 21,854 new water connections in the Pemba system, 9,021 new water connections in the Nacala system, and 13,648 new water connections in other cities under the CERC (see Annex 7). Project attribution was as noted for PDO-level Indicator 1. Information source: FIPAG SCO.

title.narrative: Number of people in urban areas provided with access to improved water sources under the project

comment.narrative: Target achieved (133%). This indicator measured the number of people who benefited from new piped household water connections, including beneficiaries of the low-income household connection program, using a 5.3 average household size as per the National Institute of Statistics. The original target was increased with the AF to reflect people in Nacala. The result reflects: 163,182 people connected to the Beira-Dondo system, 95,771 people connected to the Tete-Moatize system, 115,826 people connected to the Pemba system, and 47,811 people connected to the Nacala system, as well as 72,336 newly connected people in other cities supported under the CERC (see Annex 7). Of those newly connected, 247,958 were females using the current national average of 50.1 percent. To achieve this result, the project financed construction and installation materials, while labor was paid for by the ROCs. Information source: FIPAG Central Service for Operation (SCO).

title.narrative: Number of implemented and monitored regulatory frameworks with the regional utilities (ADM, Northern, Central and Southern)

comment.narrative: Target achieved (100%). The baseline reflects the concession agreement between FIPAG and ADM before it was incorporated as AdRMM. The four ROCs submitted performance data to AURA IP on an annual basis, and AURA IP carried out inspection and monitoring visits to the four regions on a monthly basis to verify the data. An AURANet platform was established and used to store and monitor ROCs' performance data and inform the production of performance reports, which were produced annually. The project financed the establishment of AURANet and related training on its use. Information source: AURA IP and AURANet.

title.narrative: Development and implementation of corporate equal opportunity policies/procedures (addressing gender and disability issues in particular)

comment.narrative: Target achieved (133%). The target and result reflect the number of ROCs that developed and implemented the policies/procedures. In October 2024, the Ministry of Public Works, Housing and Water Resources developed and approved a 2024-2034 National Gender Strategy for the water sector, including social inclusion. Before the Strategy was approved, FIPAG trained its planners and budgeters on integrating gender issues into planning and budgeting, and the ROCs established conceptual foundations for gender and social inclusion. Two of the ROCs (AdRC and AdRMM) hired two people with physical disabilities. Following the approval, the World Bank provided training to the regions gender focal points on gender issues and to front offices and ROCs technicians on awareness and sensitivity in serving people with physical disabilities. These actions were financed by World Bank and FIPAG resources. Information source: FIPAG Central Service for Human Resources (Servico Central de Recursos Humanos).

title.narrative: Length of water supply network laid under the project and operational (cumulative)

comment.narrative: Target substantially achieved (98%). This indicator measured the length of new functioning water supply network installed to extend coverage of and increase access to underserved areas. The target was increased with the AF to include the network laid in Nacala. The result reflects: 154.4 km in the Beira-Dondo system, 11 km in the Tete-Moatize system, 178.5 km in the Pemba system, and 183.6 km in the Nacala system. To achieve this result, the project financed material and works by contractors. Information sources: FIPAG SCO and Central Service for Projects and Investment (SCPI).

title.narrative: Audited collection ratio (annual billings less change in gross receivables)/annual billings

comment.narrative: Target partially achieved (81%). This indicator measured ROCs overall and regional annual collection ratios. The AF added an overall target (weighted average) and the targets for northern and central regions were reduced to reflect prevailing conditions. The overall result reflects the weighted average (by served population) at closing, and the regional results are based on findings of the 2024 ROC audits by independent auditors, while the 2025 audits will become available in mid-2026. See Annex 7 for more details. Information source: FIPAG SCPD.

title.narrative: Number of low-income (poor) beneficiaries of the output-based connection subsidy

comment.narrative: Target achieved (101%). This indicator tracked the number of people benefiting from the low-income household connection program. The target was reduced with the AF to remove connections in Greater Maputo. The result reflects: 49,014 people in Beira, 3,986 people in Moatize, 33,390 people in Pemba, 10,600 people in Tete, and 10,181 people in Nacala. Of those, 53,693 are females based on a national female ratio of 50.1 percent. Information source: IVA report.

title.narrative: Number of subsidized house connections with continuous water services for three months

comment.narrative: Target achieved (101%). This indicator looked at the sustainability of the poor-household connections program by measuring the number of verified connections that continued to receive service after a three-month period. The target was reduced with the AF to remove connections in Greater Maputo. All the connections were sustained for at least three months. The ROCs facilitated the households payment by allowing users to pay through installments, which has since been adopted by some of the ROCs for all types of connections. The IVA reports found that this flexibility was a key factor in poor households willingness to pay. The ROCs also established units with focal points to support the program. Information source: IVA report.

title.narrative: Number of subsidized house connections installed

comment.narrative: Target achieved (101%). This indicator tracked the result of the poor-household connection program, measuring the number of verified (by an IVA) installed connections. The target was reduced with the AF to remove connections in Greater Maputo. The result reflects: 9,248 connections in Beira, 752 in Moatize, 6,300 in Pemba, 2,000 in Tete, and 1,921 in Nacala. To achieve this result, the project financed connections materials and equipment and fee subsidies (80 percent), while the installation works were carried out by the ROCs between June 2023 and October 2024. Information sources: IVA report.

title.narrative: Commercial systems operating in regional utilities (Northern, Central & Southern)

comment.narrative: Target achieved (100%). This indicator tracked the customization or installation of a new commercial system in each utility. The systems were to include billing and commercial management functions, customer service policies and procedures, and citizen engagement and complaints handling/recourse mechanisms. In 2023, the three new ROCs customized their systems from the previously central system in FIPAG to independently operated ones, with the above functions and the ability to produce reports and performance analyses. In addition, AdRMM customized its system in 2024 with the above functions and by introducing an application to facilitate user interaction. To achieve this result, the project financed the above noted technical assistance consultancies, which carried out a baseline study and a market survey per ROC that informed system improvements. Information sources: FIPAG SCPD.

title.narrative: Increased capacity of the water systems (treatment, production, and transport)

comment.narrative: Target partially achieved (66%). This indicator measured the volume of additional water that could be treated, produced, and transported as a result of project-funded rehabilitation and expansion works. The target was increased with the AF to reflect increased production capacity in Nacala – from 7,000 m3/day to 19,000 m3/day (12,000 m3/day increase) thanks to the building of a new water treatment plant. The result reflects the following capacity increases: 10,000 m3/day in Beira-Dondo, 11,000 m3/day in Tete-Moatize, and 10,000 m3/day in Pemba. More details are available in Annex 7. Once the Nacala works are completed, 15,000 m3/day will be added to the system and almost meet the target. To achieve this result, the project financed construction and rehabilitation works. Information source: FIPAG SCPI.

title.narrative: Number of water utilities that the project is supporting

comment.narrative: Target achieved (133%). Beyond the construction and rehabilitation works, the following project-funded support was provided to the ROCs: (i) transactional advisory assistance to inform private sector engagement (all four ROCs); training in FM, human resource management, O&M and energy efficiency, commercial management, and management of non-revenue water (all four ROCs); technical assistance for the preparation of water supply master plan (AdRN); provision of performance-based grants (all four ROCs); technical and management trainings (AdRN and AdRC); gender and social inclusion trainings (AdRN, AdRC, and AdRS); and RECO training (all four ROCs). Information source: FIPAG SCPI.

title.narrative: Incorporation of regional utilities as corporations

comment.narrative: Target achieved (133%). This indicator tracked the legal creation of the regional utilities by the Council of Ministers. The four ROCs were incoporated as regional utilities by the Council of Ministers in May 2021, and their statutes were published in the Official Gazette in September 2021. Information source: FIPAG Central Service for Planning and Development (SCPD).

title.narrative: Implementation of "Citizen Voice" tools and RECO procedures in project cities

comment.narrative: Target achieved (133%). This indicator tracked the scaling up and rolling out of the RECO platform to facilitate grievance redress and recourse. This system was to include a module on grievances responded and/or resolved within a response time standard. The RECO platform was rolled out to the four regions to allow customers to submit complaints and appeals. The platform was installed on AURA IP's website and has been operating since June 2023, producing public semi-annual reports on appeals and complaints since. The system includes a module on grievances responded and/or resolved within a time standard as planned, and RECO procedures are in place. To achieve this result, the project financed a consultant that helped with the design and rolling out of the RECO and trained staff on its use and equipment, such as computers and tablets. Information sources: AURA IP.

title.narrative: Piped household water connections that are benefiting from rehabilitation works undertaken by the project

comment.narrative: Target partially achieved (35%). The target was increased with the AF to reflect connections in Nacala. The result reflects: 10,973 households in Beira-Dondo systems, 7,055 households in Tete-Moatize system, 4,300 households in the Pemba system, 600 households in the Nacala system, and 22,317 households in other cities under the CERC (see Annex 7). Project attribution was as noted for PDO-level Indicator 2. Information source: FIPAG SCO.

title.narrative: Customer satisfaction index for water supply services in the project cities

comment.narrative: Target achieved (100%). The result reflects the average satisfaction rate of a 25 percent sample of households participating in the low-income household connections program. The survey was carried out by the program's IVAs in the six participating cities. The result reflects 80 percent of households interviewed noting that they were satisfied or very satisfied with the subsidized connections installed. A project-wide satisfaction survey was not carried out at closing by AURA IP due to budget constraints. AURA IP is currently carrying out the survey with funding from the Urban Water Security Program (P178653) and the results are expected in February 2026. Information source: IVA reports.

Target partially achieved (77%). This indicator measured the population that directly benefited from new water supply connections and existing customers benefiting from rehabilitated connections, using a 5.3 average household size and a 50 percent female rate. The target was increased with the AF to reflect beneficiaries in Nacala. The result reflects the above beneficiaries, in addition to 58,157 beneficiaries of rehabilitated connections in the Beira-Dondo system, 37,392 in the Tete-Moatize system, 22,790 in the Pemba system, and 3,180 in the Nacala system. In addition, the result reflects 118,280 beneficiaries of other rehabilitation works under the CERC (see Annex 7). Of these, 368,096 were females using the current national average of 50.1 percent. To achieve this result, the project financed the construction as noted above while the rehabilitation works were financed in full by the project through contractors. Information sources: FIPAG SCO and IVA reports.

title.narrative: Number of completed and independently audited financial statements (annual)

comment.narrative: Target achieved (100%). The target and result reflect the baseline AdRMM and the three new ROCs. The financial statements were prepared by the ROCs while the independent audits were carried out annually by FIPAG-hired auditors. In 2017-2022, there were two annual audits: one for the AdRMM financial statement and one for the FIPAG financial statement, which included the three regional delegations. From 2023, the ROCs had in place separate accounts with an audited financial statement each. The 2025 statements are expected in mid-2026. To achieve this result, the project financed technical assistance to the ROCs, including hiring of two technical support companies in 2022-2024 (one for AdRC and AdRN and one for AdRS and AdRMM) that helped the ROCs define standards for data analysis, processing, and reporting based on international auditing norms, as well as training, data collection equipment, and establishment of commercial systems. Information source: FIPAG.

title.narrative: Restored production capacity in response to an emergency event

comment.narrative: Target achieved (100%). This indicator measured the production capacity affected by cyclone Idai that the project helped to restore. The target and result reflect restored capacities of 20,000 m3/day in Beira, 6,000 m3/day in Moatize, 19,000 m3/day in Tete, and 4,500 m3/day in Quelimane. To achieve the result, the project financed supply of generators for Beira's Mutua WTP's pumping station; restoration of 35 boreholes around the Niartanda River within the Tete-Moatize system that were destroyed by the cyclone, including elevation and protection of the restored boreholes; and restoration of three boreholes in Quelimane. Information sources: FIPAG's CERC completion report.
